newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria's Assad meets Lebanese PM Hariri.
newsitem.headline: Syria's Assad meets Lebanese PM Hariri.

text.p: Syrian President Hafez al-Assad had talks on Monday with Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, who is visiting to discuss regional developments and bilateral cooperation.
Presidential spokesman Joubran Kourieh said the meeting was at the presidential palace in the Syrian capital. He gave no details.
Hariri's visit is his first since the Lebanese government's announcement that a number of people suspected of involvement in violence had been detained by the security forces.
Lebanon's Saturday announcement was the first response to opposition allegations of widespread arrests of Christian opposition members.

A statement by Lebanese Prosecutor General Adnan Addoum said the detentions followed increased activities by "disruptive elements" who wanted to harm Lebanon's ties with brotherly and friendly countries, an apparent reference to Syria.

The activities included "armed attacks against civilians with hand grenades and firing with machineguns at a van carrying Syrian workers, killing the driver and wounding some passengers...distributing leaflets attacking state officials and inciting sectarian strife," Addoum said.
Syria is the main foreign power broker in Lebanon, where it has some 35,000 troops.

Officials said Hariri had talks earlier with Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam on the outcome of an international conference in Washington last week on giving economic aid to Lebanon, the situation in the region and other bilateral issues.
